requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance on node1 every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: Root's crontab contains the exact daily 02:15 entry, BusyBox crond is enabled and running, and both schedule and service recovered after restart. The command was also executed successfully as a bounded functional check, though the evidence window did not include an actual 02:15 firing.

requirements.requirement: Retain the maintenance command's output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
requirements.summary: The cron entry appends stdout and stderr to the requested log. Direct tests appended two timestamped records, and the pre-restart record remained present after restart. The log is root-owned with mode 0640.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, the platform remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. The implementation used the already-installed BusyBox/OpenRC cron components, with no package installation or upgrade shown, and package-health output was unchanged from the prepared baseline.

overall_summary: The requested daily maintenance schedule, append-only output retention, and legacy-platform preservation were achieved. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity from 61600913-2f64-409e-96d2-0e334230150e to d6ea975a-c114-4c7e-97f0-d600891e2ad3, and recovered crond, its schedule, and retained log data. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot change and unchanged platform.
limitations: The capture period did not span 02:15, so no naturally scheduled invocation was observed; scheduling is supported by the exact crontab entry, active persistent scheduler, and direct append tests.
Alpine does not provide the collector's systemd failed-unit probe, although direct OpenRC checks show crond healthy before and after restart.
The temporary restart-output file /tmp/infraset-reboot.log remained after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: configuring the cron entry and log, enabling crond, collecting bounded append evidence, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. One avoidable mutation remained: cmd-968714fd7d044e37 redirected reboot output to /tmp/infraset-reboot.log, which was still present afterward and was not needed for the demonstrated restart acknowledgement or recovery. It was not reverted, but is low-risk temporary-file residue. No other unnecessary mutation is evident; package health and network exposure were materially unchanged.
